Modern.mission: To provide serious psychotherapy on a sustainable practice model — small caseloads, long relationships, weekly cadence.

Modern.brandNameRationale: Locus is a real Latin-rooted word meaning 'place' — used in psychology in the term 'locus of control' (the perceived source of agency). Stands in the lineage of considered-modern therapy practice naming (Alma, Octave Therapy register).
Modern.manifesto: Most modern therapy companies optimize for matching speed and caseload throughput. We started Locus because the actual best therapy is slow, weekly, long-arc work with a senior therapist whose caseload is small enough to remember what you said in March. The practice is built around that work.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern mental health has split between high-volume platform-matching services (BetterHelp, Talkspace) and small considered practices. Creative.tagline: A practice built around being heard, not advised.
Creative.brandDescription: The Listening Room Co is a creative-led psychotherapy practice that positions around the quality of listening — the 50-minute uninterrupted attention that is the actual therapeutic intervention.
Creative.scope:
The Listening Room Co works across:
• Weekly 50-minute psychotherapy sessions in physically-considered rooms
• Group practice of senior therapists trained in long-arc work
• Quarterly practice essay on the craft of listening
• Sliding-scale slots on every therapist's caseload
• Annual published practice retrospective
Creative.mission: To restore listening as the primary intervention of psychotherapy.
Creative.vision: A practice whose listening rooms become a small cultural reference for what therapy is.
coreValues: Warm — the room is configured for the work.
Literary — the writing about the practice is part of the practice.
Considered — listening is the primary intervention.
Patient — the long arc is the unit of work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Listening Room is a real recording-studio trade term for the quiet, acoustically-treated room where the engineer evaluates a mix. Repurposed for a therapy practice, the phrase names the physical and metaphorical space therapy actually requires. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Modern mental health has accumulated interventions — CBT worksheets, DBT skills, EMDR protocols, exposure hierarchies, behavioural activation. All useful. Most useful inside the structure of being listened to for fifty minutes once a week. We started The Listening Room because the listening is the work. The rest is what happens because the listening happened.
Creative.industrySummary: Modern mental health marketing emphasizes evidence-based protocols and measurable outcomes. There is real space for a creative-led practice that positions on the qualitative, listening-led tradition — the part of therapy that doesn't fit on a worksheet but shows up in the long arc.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Two Chairs (twochairs.com) holds the closest peer in considered-modern practice. Octave Therapy (octave.com) plays the practice-platform peer. Alma (helloalma.com) sits in the matching-platform middle. Bloom (helloiambloom.com) plays the considered-modern niche position. We belong alongside Two Chairs with a stronger listening-led positioning.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Listening Room Co is a psychotherapy practice whose primary intervention is the 50-minute uninterrupted attention of a senior therapist.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the listening. Every aspect of the practice — the physical rooms, the therapist roster, the published essays — argues for listening as the therapeutic act.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 30-55 who have done structured therapy and want the qualitative, listening-led tradition.
behaviors: Have completed CBT or DBT programs and want something different.
Care about how the therapist actually listens.
Want a relationship rather than a protocol.
Pay full fees for the long arc.
motivations: Want a practice with a clear point of view.
Want a relationship that respects the unconscious.

dos: Publish the quarterly essay on the craft of listening.
Photograph the rooms, not the therapists.
Write therapist bios as short narratives about their training.
Send an annual printed practice retrospective.

messagingPillars.name: Listening as the intervention
messagingPillars.description: The 50-minute uninterrupted attention is the therapeutic act. Everything else — the worksheets, the protocols, the homework — is downstream of being listened to first.

messagingPillars.name: Considered rooms
messagingPillars.description: The practice's rooms are acoustically treated, warmly lit, and physically configured for face-to-face conversation. The room is part of the intervention.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: Once a quarter the practice publishes a long-form essay on the craft of listening, written by a member of the practice. The essay is the marketing.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Listening Room Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a chair beside it. The chair is the only emblem.
